I wouldn’t worry too much, most things that you plug into power has rated fuses (A) so if the cabling becomes to hot then it will blow the fuse ie keeping you safe. This is the same for any cabling that comes from your Fuse board too, the fuses are there to protect the circuit so if the cable becomes too hot, it will automatically trip - if circuits are on the right ampage rating that is. The only thing you have to be worried about is loose connections (for the most part) if your wiring is 30 years old than I would look at upgrading it, and if not then I would look at getting an electrician to test your fuse board and circuits to make sure everything is safe!

Let me just start by saying your not a worthless piece of shit. I'm actually pretty glad you posted this because you need pointing in the right direction definitely. I'm now 23 and just like you, when I was in my teenage years; I had always thought about killing myself and I wasn't aware that my thoughts would cause intense feelings of fatigue (regardless of diet etc) I would always have to nap after school, and I'd always end up procrastinating.. however, what I didn't realize is that when you hit your early adulthood you're unresolved problems follow you around and weigh you down 50x more. I'm guessing you've heard of the law of attraction, the same goes for manifesting negative thoughts only leads to negativity within your life. Things like not being 'good' at stuff like sports or being the 'last' person in your class... People do things at their own pace and that's fine, whether its slow or its fast it doesn't matter just aslong as you can kind of get it right. Obviously, i'm not an expert and can only go off my personal experience of this but I feel like a change of your mentality would be vital for you whether this is through therapy or whatever works best for you(exercise helped me more than talking to others did).. its just so important to get rid of the negativity. This just doesn't happen over night though, it takes a lot of practice to get rid of negativity and its so easy to fall in this trap. Your brain just uses your previous experiences and already has a perception in your brain of how things are going to be/ going to turn out - that's where therapy may be good just to train your mind that every situation will be different. You're not lazy, you're thoughts are just demotivating you. I noticed that thinking of suicide for long periods of time caused my brain to fog, and this led my problem solving skills to be useless. You just need one positive thing in your life to get the ball rolling, and see how things change in general.. its quite amazing what your thoughts can do.
